body.heading: A review is information, not a verdict
paragraphs: Many people avoid looking at their goals because the review feels like a judgement. But a goal that drifted is data: maybe the plan was too big, the timing was wrong, or life genuinely changed.

Set a short weekly or monthly appointment with yourself — fifteen minutes is plenty — and treat it like checking a map on a walk. You are not in trouble for being off route; you are just deciding the next turn.

body.heading: Three gentle questions
paragraphs: Ask: What moved, even slightly? What got in the way? What is the smallest next step? Writing the answers down matters, because memory edits generously in both directions.
If a goal no longer matters to you, changing or releasing it is a legitimate outcome of a review. Goals are tools for your life, not debts you owe your past self.

takeaway: Review to steer, not to scold — fifteen kind minutes is enough.
